html:
SMTO-CTR-0007 — A private or sensitive file can't be used to plan this task

GUID: 88d04b9f-2ae9-4860-a91f-c91d3496818f
Slug: task-contract-context-unavailable
Domain: CTR · Subsystem: task-contract

What happened

  • A file or item attached to this request is marked private or sensitive. SMTO won't put it into the plan it writes before working (the Task Contract), so it didn't act on this version of your request.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Find which attached file or item is marked private or sensitive, and leave it out of the request. SMTO only uses items that aren't marked private when it writes the task plan.
  2. If the task needs that information, attach a copy without the private parts using Add context, and send the request again as a new message. A copy without private content can be used for planning without exposing anything sensitive.
  3. Don't remove the item's private or sensitive marking just to get past this. That marking keeps secrets out of the plan; removing it could expose them.

What success looks like

  • The new task shows Task contract generated and starts working.

If it still fails

  • If you can't tell which item is private, or the task truly needs it, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste the private contents into your message to work around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Context admission rejected a Task Contract source because its metadata or source record is marked secure/secret or carries a classification other than public.

What this means

  • Context admission finds secure/secret metadata or a classification other than public on the source or its context record. This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.

Why this can happen

  • Context admission finds secure/secret metadata or a classification other than public on the source or its context record.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect classification metadata without copying private contents into public task text.

How to fix it

  • available_context rejected a manifest entry whose ContextStore metadata or source now carries secure/secret or a non-public classification. Use an eligible public source, or provide the material through a supported private input path; do not relabel secret material or copy its contents into task text to bypass the check.
  • Use an eligible public source or the supported private-data flow; do not relabel secret material merely to bypass this boundary.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Compilation uses supported eligible public context or the appropriate private reference flow.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
